caption: Hild on the road at 16:30 with a rounder face: a broader jaw, fuller cheeks that round off instead of ending in a cut edge, and soft folds by the mouth; the face still reads too smooth and flat at this distance, a pale scrap still shows at the collar and her forearms still read as grey plate.
Before: Hild at 16:30 with the Vanguard's chest plate cutting through her smock as a pale crescent and side strips under the hood.
After: the smock fills out below the collar so no plate shows on Hild's chest; a small linen scrap still shows at the throat, the face is still smooth and the forearms still read as grey gauntlets.

Hild at 16:30 after the villagers' kirtles lost their moth holes and their limb wraps calmed: sleeves read as even wool, but black-and-grey blotches remain on her forearms and the shin below the kirtle (likely base body poking through the wrap shells).
Before: Hild's forearms and hands read as grey mottled plate gauntlets with black blotches; pale patches on the kirtle below the girdle.

Hild's forearms now wear solid wool sleeves and mitts instead of grey gauntlets; fingers still grey glove, sleeves a touch too dark, pale thigh-plate patches still show through the side of the kirtle.

Hild's forearm and shin wraps now read as solid cloth bands: the black-and-grey camouflage blotches (undersuit poking through) are gone; the wraps are still near-black against her smock and her hands still read as grey gauntlets (rendered before 85f57b8's mitts were rebased in).

Hild at the road meeting at 16:30 with lighter shin wraps (cropped below the frame here); her forearm sleeves still read as black blocks, hands as grey gloves, and the kirtle panels are patchy and flat.

Hild at the road meeting at 16:30 with her forearm sleeves lifted to a dark brown-grey wool instead of black blocks; her fingers still read as grey gloves, the face is smooth and mask-like and the kirtle panels are patchy.
The same meeting without the chest crop: the sleeves now read as wool from elbow to wrist, but the frame still stops at her thighs, so the shin wraps go unseen, and the grey glove fingers remain.

Hild at the road meeting: her fingers now come out of the wool mitts as bare ruddy skin instead of a grey plate glove; the kirtle's front panel below the sash is still patchy rust/dark blocks and the face still reads smooth.
New full-length framing of Hild: her long kirtle and shins read as even dark wool with no pale blotches, but Wat and his creel block the lens line (framing swung to the verge side for next time).

Hild and Wat meet on the fell road, full length: her kirtle's front panel now reads as one even dark wool instead of rust and dark blocks, and the creel is out of the lens; still small in frame, faces unreadable, and the hips show a rust sleeve edge.

Hild and Wat meet on the fell road: Wat's kilted smock now reads as darker road-dun wool instead of a pale flat linen sheet; still small in frame with unreadable faces, and his chest and arms read as plated armour shapes under the creel.

Hild and Wat on the fell road: Wat's smock skirt now hangs as dun fulled road wool with a sun-faded top and damp hem instead of a flat pale linen sheet, Hild's kirtle stays even dark wool; still small in frame, faces unreadable, rust edge at her hip.

First quest: Bread for the Keep's objective corner and Hesper's quest line as a subtitle read cleanly; but the talk lens at 09:30 sits inside the keep's ivy wall, so the frame is flat ivy cards, not Hesper.

Osric's lost bellwether bell hangs by its leather collar from the last fold post under the great grey stone, quest corner and Take prompt up; still wrong: the bell is tiny in frame, the post reads as a smooth near-black pole, and there is no ruined fold round it.

The fell bell's post at the broken gateway of Osric's old fold: a ring of tumbled dry-stone wall butted against the great stone, fallen stones in the turf; still too low and dark in the backlight, a second boulder cuts through the ring, and the hero still reads stylised.

Close on the bellwether's bell, a size bigger and readable as verdigrised bronze on its strap, the post crusted with small lichen flecks; the post still reads as a smooth dark pole in shade and the grass blades are flat cards.
The old fold from down the slope at 15:00: the stray boulder no longer stands through the ring's east side, but the field stones still read near-black and the wall is low.
The fell bell on its post, now a hewn eight-sided oak quarter: the facets read, but the post is too dark in the great stone's shade, the lichen reads as pale spots and the check split doesn't show.
The old fold at 15:00 after lifting the field-stone value range: almost no change, the stones still read blue-black because the whole site stands in cast shadow and gets only cool sky ambient
Diagnostic: the fold stones in plain 0.5 grey also read flat sky-blue with no sun term, proving the near-black is cast shadow plus low masonry albedo/AO, not broken normals

The old fold at 12:00, the one hour the sun reaches it: the tumbled ring finally reads as slate-grey coursed rubble with lit tops and a broken gateway; the great stone still reads as a dark leaning slab and the light is flat
The fell bell's post at 12:00: the verdigris bell reads, but the post stands in the great stone's shadow and goes blue-black, and the lens sits in tall grass whose flat straw ribbons fill the frame

The fell bell's post at noon now reads as silvered, faceted grey oak over trodden sward instead of a blue-black pipe in straw ribbons; the great stone behind is still a featureless black mass and the light is flat.
The old fold at noon with the new sky-dome fill on shaded stone side faces: a touch lighter, the ring reads; the great stone still reads as a dark slab and the ground is flat-lit.
The great stone up the fell at noon now reads as lichened grey granite with a moss crown over the ruined fold instead of a black slab; its lower shaded flank and the fold stones are still very dark.
A meadow boulder at 14:00 with the lighter granite albedo: reads as stone now, but the sunlit face is flat and chalky with too little tonal detail.
A meadow boulder at 14:00: the sunlit face now carries broad blotches, a hand-sized mottle and shaded fissures instead of one chalky sheet; the shaded side is still near-black.
Close crop of the same boulder: the lit face reads as weathered, stained granite with moss in its hollows; the shadow side is still a black mass.

A meadow boulder at 14:00 with the new sky-dome floor: the shaded flank now reads as cool grey granite with its cracks and moss instead of a black mass; it is a touch blue and the scene's light is still flat.
The same boulder before this session's change, for comparison: the face turned from the sun is near-black, darker than the shaded grass beside it.
The old fold at noon with the sky floor on its field stones: the shaded wall faces read as grey rubble instead of black; the stones are still blocky slabs and the light is flat.
A meadow boulder at 14:00 with the warmed sky floor: the shaded flank is neutral grey granite instead of a blue cast; the stone still sits in a flat, lifeless meadow.
The old fold at noon: its field stones are now irregular lumps with knocked-off corners instead of squared slabs; still too bluish-grey and small, and the light is flat.
The old fold at noon with bigger, warmer field stones and through-stones: the ring reads as a real tumbled wall now, but the stones still look cool grey with chalky lit edges and the light is flat.

The new wheatears on the old fold's wall tops at 10:00, cock (grey, black mask) on the cope stone left of centre, hen beyond; still wrong: they are small and easy to miss in a still, the folded black wing barely shows, and the lens meant to frame the cock close landed on the wall instead.

Crop of the same frame: the cock's grey back, mask, white brow and dark tail and the buff hen read as real small birds on the stones; still wrong: no visible closed wing on the flank, tail edge-on like a stick, feather detail soft.

The Ashen Knight's phase 3 in the meadow: boss bar with phase notches, the ember-ring warning before an eruption under the hero. Still wrong: the ring reads as a flat orange circle, not burning turf, and the knight is a recoloured soldier with no armour of its own.

Phase 3 of the Ashen Knight: an eruption bursting under the hero, now captured at the burst. Still wrong: the flame column is an over-bright additive blob that whites out the frame and hides the new scorch decal, and the knight still has no armour of its own.

The Ashen Knight's phase-3 eruption is now a narrow column of flame tongues with dark smoke instead of a white blob; still wrong: the low camera hides the scorch in the grass, the practice post blocks the hero, and the knight is still a re-tinted soldier.

First look at the Ashen Knight's armour: the helm, pauldrons and burnt oxblood surcoat give it a boss silhouette with the ember burning through the chest; still wrong: the frame is backlit so the steel reads as black, the helm is a small round cap, the pauldron sits like a hump and the glaive looks thin.

First look at the Ashen Knight's standing-stone ring at golden hour: the ring and the entrance gap read, but the stones are thin posts, not sarsens (enlarged afterwards, unseen), the burnt ground is hidden under the tall grass, and the knight is a speck at its post.

The Ashen Knight's stone ring in low sun: the stones now stand as broad, tall sarsens and the tall grass inside is gone, but the floor still reads as green turf because the scorch decals don't show, and the knight is small at this distance.
The knight's stone ring: the burnt ground finally shows inside the sarsens, but it reads as a bluish wet slab or puddle with a too-clean round edge rather than dry ash and charred stubble.

The knight's stone ring: the burn now reads as dry warm grey-brown ash with soil showing and a ragged edge instead of a wet slab, but the centre char patch still looks like a dark hole, the meadow still stops fairly sharply at the ash, and the knight is a speck at this range.

The Ashen Knight close up with the camera finally on the sun side: the meadow and the hero are front-lit and the ember-cracked helm and oxblood surcoat read, but the knight is turned to the hero so we see its dark back, and the boss bar covers its legs.

The Briar Hound pair on the meadow east side: one crouched mid-tell in front of the hero, but it reads as a dark blob sunk in the tall grass and its mate is out of frame; needs pressed grass under the hounds and a closer, lower camera.

The Briar Hounds now read against the meadow (smoke-grey coat, a pressed lane of grass behind the runner, its mate crouched behind the hero), but the grizzle comes out as leopard-like speckles and the hero's staff still looks slung.

The near Briar Hound's coat now reads as streaky grizzled guard hair over smoke-grey (no more leopard speckles) as it lopes past the hero; still wrong: the crouched mate is lost in the far grass, the hounds' silhouettes are smooth (no thorny ruff) and the hero's guard holds the staff high like a yoke.

The hero's new mid guard: staff held low and diagonal across the body instead of yoked over the shoulders; still wrong: the hero is in shade, the straw post crowds the frame and the shaft's middle hides behind the arm.

Hero in the low mid guard, re-shot from the sun side: lit, whole staff visible, no yoke -- but from this near-frontal angle the shaft reads level across the hips rather than diagonal, the face under the hat is a dark blank and the straw post still crowds the right.

Hero in the mid guard from the raised sun-side lens: lit and the whole staff shows, but with only -12 deg of pitch the shaft still reads as a level bar across the belly and the face is a blank grey cloth.

Hero in the new low guard: the staff now reads as a clear diagonal, tip down to knee height -- but the figure still looks squat and toy-like, the face is a blank grey cloth and the straw post crowds the right.
The hero's douli cut to a man's 0.58 m: he no longer reads as a toy under a parasol, but the hood and face cloth still read as a flat grey box round the head and the torso is bulky over hidden legs.

The hero's head after the jaw taper: hood and face cloth now narrow from the temples to the throat so it reads as a head with eyes, not a grey box; still wrong: the face cloth's dark tail hangs below the hood's pale ragged collar over the breastplate, and the skin reads doll-smooth.
The hero's face cloth now ends inside the hood's lower edge instead of hanging a dark tail onto the breastplate; still wrong: the armour reads dark and flat and the hood is a plain grey shell.

The hero in the low guard after the sash was cut to a hand's breadth (11 cm) and the face cloth tucked: the waist reads as a belt, not a girdle, but the hood still reads as a dark grey block from this angle, the figure is squat over hidden legs and the staff's bright red lacquer looks toy-like.

Hero in the mid guard at 15:00: the staff is now a deep oxblood lacquer with worn wood showing near the grips instead of a toy-bright red; the hood still reads as a grey block and the figure is lost in tall grass.

Hero in the mid guard at 15:00 after the hood was warmed and creased down the cheeks: barely visible at this range -- the head still reads as a grey block because the face cloth covers the whole front, and the figure is lost in tall grass.

Hero close-up after the face cloth was dropped under the nose: the hood now frames a face with a nose, cheekbones and eyes instead of a grey block, but the skin reads as a smooth orange mannequin and the cloth front is a flat dark panel.
The new Hollow Hewer (left) holds its felling axe overhead at the top of the chop with the glint on the bit; GL quick frame, the figure is backlit and dark and the axe head reads small.
The hewer bent over its buried axe after the hero rolled clear (GL quick frame); the new turf burst reads as a flat over-bright smear on the ground and the camera framing is off.

GL frame looking down on the Hewer's missed chop: the turf burst is now a soft, shaded brown haze with dark soil crumbs instead of a pale glowing smear; the hewer still stands upright instead of bent over the buried bit, and the frame is GL, dark and shadowed.

The Hollow Hewer bent ~40 deg over its buried axe after a dodged chop, arms down the helve into the turf (the punish window now reads); still GL, the bit itself is lost in the grass and dust and the hood reads as a smooth green sack.

The Hollow Hewer bent over its buried axe with the grass laid flat round the bit and a low, short dust; its hood is now creased brown wool. Still GL, and the near grass plus the house shadow swallow the figure.
The new Ashen Archer (left, red hood) at full draw, bow arm out at the hero; GL quick frame, the archer stands in the house's shadow so the bow and draw are hard to read, still needs a Forward+ look.

An Ashen Archer's arrow lodged in the hero's chest after a hit, fletching out, the archer at the left edge; GL quick frame, the impact dust puff is too bright and pale, and the in-flight streak still does not read in the side-on flight frame.

GL frame: the fletched half of an arrow the hero rolled on lies across a patch of pressed-flat sward; the shaft reads only as a dark hairline in this light and the pale wood-chip hit FX still float above the grass.

An archer's arrow standing in the hero's chest now reads as pale ash with grey-goose fletching instead of a dark hairline; GL compatibility frame, flat light, the field still lacks Wukong-grade density.
The fletched half of a snapped arrow lies on the pressed grass and is visible at last (it used to sink below the terrain grid); GL frame, the half is small and the near grass clumps are flat-lit.
The Ashen Archer on its new post, a knoll at the wood's edge clear of the trunks, seen from the hero's flank down the slope; GL frame, and the archer is lost in the wood's shadow and the long grass.

The Ashen Archer now waits on a sunlit rise at the wood's edge and reads clearly against the meadow; the hero in the foreground is still a dark silhouette in the oak shadow and the archer is small in frame.

An Ashen Archer's arrow in flight, framed square-on: grey-goose fletching, pale ash shaft and iron head cross the tree line toward the hero. Still wrong: GL render, the hero has their back to the shot, and the streak is faint against the pale sky.

GL quick look at dusk: a Hollow Wisp at the peak of its flare (an ember-veined coal in a ring of charred shards) over the meadow past the hero; still wrong: it is small at 5 m, its two kin do not read at all, and this is GL light, not Forward+.

A doused Hollow Wisp knot in a downpour on the meadow: wet turf, puddles and rain streaks read well, but the steam off the coals barely shows, the flaring heart is still a bright ball, the shards read as flat orange flakes and the hero is out of frame

A doused Hollow Wisp knot in the rain, framed over the hero's shoulder: blacker char shards and a pale steam plume off the flaring coal now read, with a kin wisp glowing past his shoulder; the wisps are still small at 4 m, the hero's back is a flat dark shape, and this is a GL frame, not Forward+.

Night: the Hollow Wisp knot drawn in off the meadow, wheeling in the smoke over Hesper's fire while she dozes beside it (GL frame) -- the coals still read as big bright balls and the ivy is flat yellow; Hesper does not react to them yet.

Forward+ night frame of the wisp knot wheeling over Hesper's fire: the keep's firelit stone and the night sky read well, but the wisp hearts blow out to flat cream discs with no veins, the fire's smoke is a dark blob and Hesper is lit cold blue.

Forward+ night: the three wisp hearts over Hesper's fire now show a cracked veined coal face instead of flat cream discs, but the crust plates still read pale grey, the fire smoke is a dark blob and Hesper is lit cold blue.

Hesper backed against the keep's inner face with both hands up, warding off the Hollow Wisps wheeling over her fire (GL fallback): the fear reads, but the frame is very dark, her hands read pale as gloves, the right forearm never crosses her face and the knot itself is out of frame.

Hesper backed against the keep wall from the Hollow Wisps, her right forearm now raised to her face (GL fallback frame; Vulkan failed): the lens sees her from behind, her hands are chalk white and the knot is out of frame.

The Stone Sentinel's glaive slam just landed (GL frame): blade bitten in the turf, the hero thrown by the shock; but the dust reads as sparse yellow blobs, the shock ring does not read as a ring, and the crack decal is invisible (decals need Forward+, and the tall grass hides the ground).

Stone Sentinel's glaive bitten into the turf after the slam (GL frame): the sward now lies flat in a dark ring round the pit, but the new dust ring is lost in the tree shade (too dark, too thin) and the statue still reads chalk white.
The Stone Sentinel on its new carved two-step granite plinth: squared, tooled blocks, but the plinth sits in deep shade, the lens is behind the statue and GL renders the statue chalk white.
From 12 m down the meadow the Sentinel now reads as a statue on a plinth, not a man in a field; the plinth is a dark lump in shade and the frame is the dim GL fallback.

The Stone Sentinel's slam at noon: the pale dust ring now reads clearly running out over the sward with the hero thrown down, but in full sun it is too white and glowy, a pale half-dome card sits at the pit and the statue is chalk white in GL.
The Ashen Knight 1.7 m up in its new ember leap over the meadow (GL frame); it reads as floating: the legs hang straight with no tuck and the glaive is upright at its side instead of heaved overhead.

The Ashen Knight at the top of its ember leap, knees tucked under it and the glaive heaved over its helm with the blade laid back; still a GL-compat frame (dark sky, flat distant mountains), and the cape hangs stiff instead of streaming.

The Ashen Knight coming down out of its ember leap, knees tucked, the oxblood back tabard flared out behind on the air; still wrong: GL fallback sky and chalky mountains, the front panel barely reads, no scorch where the glaive will bite.

The Ashen Knight's glaive bitten into the turf after its ember leap: the meadow grass blasted flat in a ring round the bite, ember glow and sparks lifting off it; still wrong: GL fallback frame, the black char barely shows through the laid grass (the stems should scorch too), and the practice post crowds the framing.

The Ashen Knight's leap scorch 8 s on (GL frame): the grass and soil inside the bite are now charred black in a ragged burnt star with sooted stubble; the practice post still crowds the foreground and the frame is not Forward+.

The new Hollow Harrier crouched at the hero's back with the spear low and the glint at its point (GL frame): the crouch reads, but it is lost in shade and the practice post crowds the foreground; reframe from the lit side.

The Hollow Harrier's new lean cut in its crouch: fitted hemp coif over the helm, bare narrow pale shoulders, short brown kilt, spear low with the glint at the point; the coif is still a smooth sack with no visible wrap turns or tails from this side, and this is a GL fallback frame, not Forward+.

Hollow Harrier crouched with its coif now wound in spiral strips and a knotted tail at the nape; the even thin turns make the head read like a clay pot, and GL-compatibility lighting is flat (no Forward+ frame).

GL frame from behind the Hollow Harrier's shoulder: the coif's turns now run wide and narrow with dark laps, but the head still reads as a smooth pot, the camera sits too high and close, and the loose end and nape tails are hidden behind the shoulder.

The Hollow Kindler mid-chant at dusk, spear raised, pouring a thick ember stream into the white-hot shield Warden beside the hero (GL frame); the stream now reads, but both Hollows stand as dark backlit silhouettes and the motes look scattered rather than a flowing ribbon.

The Hollow Kindler mid-chant at 16:30 pouring a tight ember stream with a hot thread under it into the kindled Warden (GL frame): the stream finally reads as one ribbon across the meadow, but the thread looks laser-straight and both Hollows still stand in shade with their backs half to the lens.

The Hollow Kindler mid-chant at 17:00 (GL frame): the ember thread now hangs in a soft wavering arc instead of a laser line, but the motes still flew straight above it (fixed after the frame: they now fall along the same arc), the thread leaves its chest not the spear tip, and the Kindler still shows its back.

The Hollow Kindler mid-chant from its front quarter (GL frame, 17:00): the ember thread now leaves the point of the raised spear about 3 m up, but the motes arced high above the thread (a sign error in their launch, fixed and re-rendered in the next shot).

After the fix: the motes now pour down the same hanging thread from the spear point to the kindled ally off-frame; still wrong: the Kindler stands backlit in shadow so its face does not read, the warden it kindles is out of shot, and the sky is blotchy.

The Kindler shot reframed from the sunlit side and backed off: the ember thread now pours from the raised spear point down to the warden, both readable in one frame; still wrong: at 16:00 a long cast shadow drowns the foreground and both Hollows into silhouette, and a lantern-post lamp hangs into the top-left corner.

Same Kindler shot at 14:30: both Hollows and the kindled warden stand in daylight with the ember thread pouring from the spear tip down to the warden along the rut road; still wrong: the Kindler's hood hides its face from this side-on lens, a lantern-post lamp hangs into the top-left, and the Hollows' cloth still reads coarse.

Hollow Kindler at 14:30 with the lantern post swung out of frame and its ember thread pouring from the spear tip; still wrong: it reads from behind with the hood hiding its face, the kindled warden is off the right edge, and a cottage shadow blacks out the bottom third.

The Hollow Kindler now chants into the sun, front-lit, with its face under the hood and the ember stream pouring from its spear tip; but the hero fills the right third and the burning warden is off the right edge.

Kindler close-up with the hero moved behind the lens: the white-hot kindled warden with glowing cracks fills the foreground and the Kindler chants behind it, the ember thread joining spear tip to warden; still wrong: the warden's sackcloth hood and tabard read flat and coarse at this range, and the GL frame shows square spark sprites.

Kindled warden up close in the meadow: its hood, mantle and tabard now hang in irregular drape folds with visible slubbed hemp threads and soft darns instead of flat sacking; still wrong: the tabard and sash panels are flat-cut geometry with straight silhouettes, and GL draws square spark sprites.
Kindled warden up close: the tabard now hangs in real uneven pleats with a torn side edge and ragged hem; still GL-only, square spark sprites, and the shoulder mantle reads as a stiff box.

Kindled warden close-up: the shoulder mantle now drapes in uneven folds from the shoulders with a torn front edge and hand-cut hem instead of a stiff cone; still GL-only (square spark sprites) and the hood reads heavy.

Kindled warden close-up: the Hollow cowl now has a thick rolled brim round the face, drape folds deepening to the shoulders and a torn edge; the crown is still a smooth dome and GL draws square sparks.

Kindled warden close-up: the cowl crown now gathers into a slumped peak pulled back over the skull with creases running down from it instead of a smooth dome; still a GL frame with square spark sprites.

The crouched harrier's hand-wound coif close up: uneven strip laps, a strip over the crown and a tie-off knot break the old smooth pot shape; still a GL frame, and the white ember-cracked armour and small head read busy.

Harrier up close: the ash-stone skin is now dull grey with sooty blotches and broken, irregular dark seams instead of a chalk-white honeycomb; still GL only, and the chest glow is busy during the tell.
A Hollow Soldier mid wind-up: the chest tell is now dark ash with a few broken burning cracks and a soft underglow instead of a lit honeycomb; GL quick-look only, no Forward+ fog/bloom.

Crouched harrier from behind (GL frame): helm lugs no longer poke through the coif and the neck is bound, but an orange-lit patch remains on the nape (likely the ember light, unculled in GL) and the knot does not read.

Crouched harrier from behind mid wind-up (GL frame): the orange glow on the nape is gone (the chest band no longer follows the crouch onto the back), but a thin ember sliver still shows at the lower-back edge and the frame is GL, not Forward+.
Hollow spearman winding up, seen from the front (GL frame): the chest still smoulders through broken cracks during the tell after the facing fix; backlit and GL-only, so the burn has no bloom.

The Ashen Knight at its phase-1 size (~2.5x the hero) beside the hero, boss bar with phase notches (GL quick-look): the size reads but it is a GL frame, not at its stone ring, and the knight's ember skin is dark.

The Ashen Knight at its phase-3 size (~5.3x the hero) towering over the small hero (GL quick-look): the giant reads, but the camera is too close to compare sizes cleanly and there is no growth FX in frame.
Boss reveal, first shot: the lens low at the Ashen Knight's feet as it cranes up the giant; GL frame, no letterbox in this render, and the knight is a dark backlit silhouette.

Boss reveal, roar beat: letterboxed, the giant brandishes its glaive skyward with the ember blazing at its shoulders; still GL, backlit against the sun, and the arms do not rise high enough for a roar.

Phase-2 Ashen Knight with the right knee raised high for the stomp, the hero small in front; GL frame, the giant is backlit so the lifted leg reads only as a silhouette and the body leans back stiffly.

Phase-3 stomp: a dust wall racing out over the meadow to the hero and the stamped ground burning under the giant; GL frame, the burning patch reads as a dark disc with a dome of flame, not yet a convincing ground fire.
The Ashen Knight's stone ring widened to ~32 m with 4-6 m uprights so the growing giant has room; GL fallback frame (Forward+ ran out of memory), the ash floor reads too dark and flat.
The hero at the top of a held running jump over the meadow (GL frame): knees tucked, robe flared; the air pose is still a procedural squat with splayed hands, no mocap clip.
Rising out of a running jump, 0.7 m up, legs gathering under the hips (GL frame); reads as a jump but stiff, the arms only swing forward.

The Ashen Knight 0.6 s into its growth in the stone ring: embers spitting from the pauldron seams, dust kicked up round its feet (GL frame, backlit at 15:00; the grit falling off the stones barely reads and the knight is a silhouette).

1.3 s into the growth: the ring of fire up round the swelling knight, small orange sparks off its armour, cracks glowing on the plate (GL frame; the surge's stone-chip burst still reads as pale snow over the helm).
The new jump attack at its top: the staff hauled straight overhead with the legs tucked, about to come down on the practice post (GL frame; procedural pose, no mocap clip, figure small in frame).

The new plunging attack at impact: the ferrule driven into the turf beside the post, hands high on the shaft (GL frame; the body still reads fairly upright and the soil burst is not caught in this frozen frame).

The Ashen Knight 1 s into its growth: the opening burst is now dark ash and a short ember spit instead of 15 m of pale chips; the ring of fire reads, but a thin pale speck column still rises behind the helm (not this burst) and it is a GL frame with a small figure.
The hero 0.3 s after a plunge from 4 m: a low dust ring bursts out round the deep crouch; GL frame, backlit in the cottage's shadow, and the crack star is hidden under the standing grass.

The Ashen Knight starting to grow from inside its stone ring, the sky above it now clear: the column of pale 'snow' specks was fog being added over the keep's additive thermal chaff. Still a GL frame; the knight's heave is only a knee pose.

New low flank view one second into the phase-2 growth: charred ash flakes drift up dark against the sky and the ring of fire stands round the knight. GL frame taken before the flame shader's fog fix; the flames still look like flat sprites.

Jump take-off, 1/60 s after the press (GL): the hero is drawn low with the soles still on the turf, pushing out of a crouch. The lens is from behind rather than the side, and the feet are too dark to check the toes.

Jump 0.1 s in (GL): legs driven straight, an arm thrown up with the elbow bent, before the tuck. The pose reads, but it is a procedural layer over the clip with no mocap take-off, and the hero is backlit and small.
Kick off the keep face 0.1 s in (GL): hands flung up off the holds as the body starts to twist away. Still reads upright from this lens; no planted-sole kick, and the hero is small in frame.
Kick off the keep face 0.25 s in (GL): twisted round to face the flight, knees gathering, staff on the back. The leap reads, but it is a procedural pose over the clip with no mocap.

The hero 0.15 s into a kick off the keep's face above the scree heap (GL quick look); loose stones like these no longer give a false catch, but the kick still reads as an upright stand with raised arms, not legs driving off the stones.

The hero dropped onto the Ashen Knight's helm in the stone ring (GL quick look, hand-stepped): the crown strike works in play and in the bot, but this frame catches the hero upright before the plunge, seen from behind the giant, not the flank; no dedicated reel pose yet.
GL quick-look: the crowned Ashen Knight 0.45 s into its reel, knees buckled, glaive drooped blade-first into the turf; still a backlit silhouette, the bowed head barely reads, not Forward+.
GL quick-look: the knight shaking the crown strike off at 1.05 s, head thrown back, ember cracks flaring; backlit, little surface detail, not Forward+.
